summary: The single biggest source of exam questions (Block C) — conduit fill, box/pull-box fill, cover depths, bend radius and cable rules dominate. Most of these are pure table lookups, so speed and the right table choice decide pass/fail here.

mustKnow: Fill %: 1 conductor→53%, 2→31%, 3 or more→40% (Table 8). Conduit-fill engine = Table 10 (areas) + Table 8 (fill %) + Table 6/9 (conduit size); bonding conductor IS counted in conduit fill.

Box fill (CEC ≠ NEC): a device (receptacle/switch) counts as ONE conductor of the largest size; the bonding/ground conductor adds NO separate volume; wire connectors are NOT each counted like in the NEC.
Pull boxes (12-3036): straight pull = 8× largest raceway trade size; angle or U pull = 6× largest + sum of the other raceways entering the same wall.
Max bends between pull points = 4 × 90° = 360° (12-940). Bend radius is read from Table 7 by conduit trade size, not the conductor.
Underground cover (Table 53): ≤750 V unprotected = 600 mm non-vehicular / 900 mm vehicular; mechanical protection (plank/concrete) reduces cover by 150 mm.
Cable through studs: keep 32 mm from the outer edge (12-516) or fit a steel protector plate; min 150 mm free conductor at each box (12-3014).
Voltage ratings: NMD90 = 300 V, AC90 ≤ 2000 V, TECK90 ≤ 5000 V. Parallel only #1/0 and larger (12-108).
Support: secure within 300 mm of a box, then ≤1.5 m for cable/armoured (12-510/12-618). NMSC clearances 25 mm heat pipe / 50 mm chimney.
No splices inside conduit (12-912); PV conductors not in same raceway as other systems (12-904). Box set-back ≤6 mm in non-combustible surfaces, flush in combustible.
traps: Box fill: counting the bonding conductor as a separate volume (it is NOT in the CEC) or counting each wire connector as a conductor like the NEC — both inflate the answer.
Wrong fill %: using 53% or 31% when there are 3+ conductors — almost always 40% on real exam questions.
Pull box: applying 8× (straight) when the entries are at an angle/U (should be 6× + sum of others) or vice-versa — read the diagram carefully.
Bend radius from Table 7 is keyed to the CONDUIT trade size, not the conductor being pulled in.
Cover depth: forgetting the 150 mm reduction with mechanical protection, or confusing it with the 38 mm plank / 50 mm concrete thickness values.
Voltage: picking 600 V for NMD90 — it is 300 V. 'EMT is NOT a conduit' wording can flip a fill/bend answer.
Counting a balanced neutral or bonding conductor when sizing for fill — bond IS counted in conduit fill but NOT in box fill (opposite rules).
Conduit expansion: forgetting ΔT spans below zero (e.g. -50 to +25 = 75°C, not 25).
mnemonic: Fill counts down the road: 1-lane 53, 2-lane 31, 3+-lane 40. Pull boxes: STraight = 8 (eight letters in 'straight-ish'), angle/U = 6.
method: Conduit fill: (1) Table 10 → area of each conductor, sum all; (2) Table 8 → fill % by count (3+ = 40%); (3) Table 6/9 → smallest conduit whose allowable area ≥ total. Reverse for 'how many fit.'
Box fill: count conductors entering + 1 per device (largest size) — ignore bond volume and connectors; multiply Table 22 mL × equivalents, or read Table 23 directly.
Pull box: identify straight vs angle/U pulls per the diagram; straight wall = 8× largest, angle/U wall = 6× largest + sum of other entries on that wall.
Cover/bend/voltage/clearance: pure lookup — go straight to Table 53 / Table 7 / Table D1 / Rule 12-510 and read the matching row.
Expansion: ΔT = max − min temp; expansion = Table 38 coeff × length (m) × ΔT.

name: Overcurrent Protection
summary: Fewer questions but high-value and predictable — the ground-fault-protection 'both conditions' rule and basic overcurrent sizing recur almost every exam. Most are one-step rule lookups, so these are easy marks if you know the two thresholds cold.

keyTables.use: Pick the standard breaker/fuse size at or below conductor ampacity
Get ampacity first, then size the OCPD to it (14-104)

keyRules.note: Required ONLY if BOTH ≥1000 A AND >150 V to ground; must clear ≥3000 A within 1 s
≤ conductor ampacity; if no standard size matches, next LOWER standard (with permitted exception to next higher)

keyRules.what: Overcurrent protection required for each conductor
keyRules.note: Foundation rule — every ungrounded conductor protected
Device must safely interrupt available fault current
Default 10 000 A symmetrical unless marked higher
Tungsten ('T') rated for incandescent; knife switch limits

mustKnow: GFP rule (14-102): equipment ground-fault protection required ONLY when BOTH conditions are true — service rated 1000 A or more AND more than 150 V to ground. 208Y/120 V (120 V to ground) never qualifies; 600/347 V qualifies only at ≥1000 A.
GFP clearing time: a ground-fault current of 3000 A or more must be cleared within a maximum of 1 second (14-102).
Overcurrent vs overload: overcurrent (fuse/breaker, Section 14) protects the CONDUCTORS; overload (thermal, Section 28) protects the MOTOR — the single most-confused exam pair.

OCPD sizing (14-104): device rating ≤ conductor ampacity; where ampacity doesn't equal a standard size, use the next LOWER standard size from Table 13 (a permitted exception allows next higher for non-continuous loads ≤ certain ratings).
Breaker default interrupting rating = 10 000 A symmetrical unless specifically marked otherwise (14-606); plug fuse max = 30 A (14-200).
traps: GFP: answering 'Yes' when only ONE of the two conditions is met — high current at low voltage (2000 A, 208 V) or high voltage at low current (800 A, 347 V) both = NO.
Confusing overcurrent (protects wire) with overload (protects motor) — they are different sections and different sizing bases.
Sizing the breaker to the LOAD instead of the CONDUCTOR ampacity, or rounding UP to next standard size when 14-104 calls for next lower.
Assuming a higher interrupting rating than the 10 000 A default just because voltage/frame size is large.
Treating 150 V to ground as exclusive — '>150 V' means 347 V qualifies but 150 V itself does not.
mnemonic: GFP needs the GRAND SLAM: 1000 A AND 150 V — BOTH bases or you're OUT (no GFP).
method: Ground-fault protection: check BOTH gates — is it ≥1000 A? AND is it >150 V to ground? Only 'yes' to both → GFP required. Either 'no' → not required.
Conductor overcurrent: (1) Table 2/4 → conductor ampacity; (2) Rule 14-104 → set OCPD ≤ that ampacity; (3) Table 13 → nearest standard size (next lower unless exception applies).
Device rating questions (plug fuse, knife switch, interrupting rating): straight rule lookup — go to 14-200 / 14-510 / 14-606 and read the limit.
